officialLinks.label: GPA calculation examples and undergraduate/graduate U distinction
Transfer admission and transfer GPA rules

helpIntro: Texas A&M undergraduates use a 4.0 scale: A=4, B=3, C=2, D=1, and F/U=0. Enter semester credit hours and final grades for a planning estimate.
helpNote: For College Station undergraduate institutional GPA. S, W, Q, I, NG and X are excluded. Graduate GPA rules differ, and Repeat Impact is unavailable because Texas A&M does not use simple grade replacement.
helpExample: A 3-hour A earns 12 grade points and a 4-hour B earns 12. Together, 24 ÷ 7 = 3.429.

gradeExplanations.A: A = 4 points per semester credit hour.
gradeExplanations.B: B = 3 points per semester credit hour.
gradeExplanations.C: C = 2 points per semester credit hour.
gradeExplanations.D: D = 1 point per semester credit hour.
gradeExplanations.F: F = 0 points; attempted hours count in GPA.
gradeExplanations.U: Undergraduate U affects GPA like F: zero points and attempted hours count.
gradeExplanations.NG: No Grade is excluded from GPA.
gradeExplanations.X: No grade submitted; excluded until resolved.
gradeExplanations.F*: Honor Code F*: zero points; hours count in GPA.
gradeExplanations.U*: Honor Code U*: zero points; hours count in GPA.

specialTypes.name: Texas A&M course
specialTypes.note: Use for standard undergraduate Texas A&M coursework.

specialTypes.name: External transfer course
specialTypes.note: Transfer grades do not enter the Texas A&M institutional GPA.

specialTypes.name: Repeat after original A or B
specialTypes.note: A repeat after a B or better has a special no-grade-points rule; confirm transcript/GPA treatment with the registrar before calculating.

repeatPolicy.note: Repeat Impact is unavailable. For ordinary eligible repeats below B, enter each graded attempt separately; if the original grade was A or B, use manual review.
